rejected.title: Kublai Khan and Yuan China
card: Kublai Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan. He became the Great Khan, the ruler of the Mongol Empire, in the 1260s.
In 1271 Kublai named his rule the Yuan dynasty, and by 1279 he had conquered all of China. A dynasty is a line of rulers from one family.
Mongols were a small group among a huge Chinese population. Kublai used Mongol officials in the highest government jobs to keep control.
Kublai moved his capital to Dadu, on the site of modern Beijing. The Yuan dynasty ruled China until 1368.
rejected.remember: Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty, took all of China and kept Mongol officials in the top jobs.

a.q: Who founded the Yuan dynasty in China?
opts: Kublai Khan, a grandson of Genghis Khan
Genghis Khan, who conquered all of China himself
Marco Polo, who came to rule China
A Chinese emperor who drove out the Mongols
a.why: Kublai Khan, Genghis Khan's grandson, named his rule the Yuan dynasty in 1271 and finished conquering China by 1279. Genghis Khan is the tempting answer, but it was his grandson who founded the Yuan dynasty.
a.clue: The founder was a grandson of the first great Khan.

b.q: Kublai Khan ruled a Chinese population far larger than the Mongol people. Which choice best fits how he governed China?
opts: He placed Mongol officials in top government jobs
He handed top government jobs only to local Chinese
He left China to rule itself under its old dynasty
He moved his capital away from China altogether
b.why: Mongols were few compared with the Chinese, so Kublai used Mongol officials in the highest jobs to keep control. Leaving China to its old rulers is tempting, but Kublai conquered China and ruled it himself as the Yuan dynasty.
b.clue: Think about who held the top jobs and who kept control.

problems.detail: The card says Kublai conquered all of China and then, in 1271, named the Yuan dynasty. This order is wrong: he proclaimed the Yuan in 1271 but did not finish conquering the Southern Song until 1279. Reword, for example: 'In 1271 he named his rule the Yuan dynasty, and by 1279 he had conquered all of China.'
Why (a) says Kublai 'conquered China, then founded the Yuan dynasty'. That gets the order backwards: the Yuan was founded in 1271 and the conquest was completed in 1279.
